newsitem.title: INDIA: Jammu and Kashmir forms human rights panel.
newsitem.headline: Jammu and Kashmir forms human rights panel.

text.p: The three-month-old government of India's rebellious Jammu and Kashmir state has decided to set up a human rights commission to investigate rights abuses, a senior official said on Tuesday.

But the panel, which would be the first such state-level commission in India, would not be empowered to examine alleged abuses by the army, which has thousands of soldiers in the Himalayan region to combat a separatist insurgency.

The decision to establish the commission was taken by chief minister Farooq Abdullah's cabinet at a meeting late on Monday in the state's winter capital Jammu, said the official, who asked not to be named.
Abdullah was appointed chief minister in October following the first assembly elections in the state since the separatist revolt broke out in 1990.
International human rights groups have accused both security forces and militants of human rights abuses in Kashmir.

The National Human Rights Commission, formed by the federal government in 1993 under pressure from Western nations, accused Jammu and Kashmir authorities in September of concealing reports of rights abuses by security forces there.
Jammu and Kashmir Governor K.V. Krishna Rao, a former Indian army chief, has acknowledged that there have been some abuses by soldiers, but said they have been few and the guilty have been punished.

During assembly elections in September and parliamentary polls in May, authorities accused militants, who boycotted the elections, of threatening voters. Separatists said security forces constrained some voters to cast ballots.
Since Abdullah took office in October, the army has been given a more active role in combatting insurgency.

Abdullah's cabinet had decided that a state-level human rights panel could not be empowered to investigate alleged abuses by the army as defence matters were controlled by the federal government in New Delhi, the senior official said.
